title: Canonical form and row edits
note: tad canon (declared field order, empty as null, row order kept, only on checked data) and tad set (one row added or updated, typed by its declaration, the whole repository re-checked, the file put back if anything would break). Proven byte for byte: canon changes nothing Python wrote; on messy copies of all four repositories Python's canon and tad's write identical files; an edit and an insertion by Python's SQL and by tad set write identical files.

title: tad check, in Rust
note: tad check: rows (types, required, allowed values, patterns, prefixes, ranges, differing pairs, dependencies, keys) and rules across tables (unique ids, references, appears-in, no mirrored relations). Same verdicts as Python's canon and checks on all four repositories and on sixteen broken copies.

title: Tables declared as data
note: All four repositories keep a tables.toml at their root: tables generated from schema.sql, rules across tables written by hand from checks/*.sql, each giving the same verdicts as Python on the real data and on broken copies.

title: Every marked project keeps its data with tad
note: The heart of oco-eco: every project's state as text as data, gathered and propagated.

title: The formats and protocols
note: Text as data: tables as JSON lines with a schema, the canonical form, verification.

title: Data gathered automatically from real files and tests
note: Today ad hoc in linux-phone-oco/docs: three scheduled feeds (wiki claims, kernel activity, shell releases) and device test results imported. Next: gatherers as standard CI jobs and hooks that tad itself brings. Parked 2026-11-11: tad's duties move into ocoeco; this returns there.

title: tad in Rust - general, Python-free
note: The text/file database in git, kept general: schemas with typed columns and allowed values, canonical form, documents rendered from data, queries - in Rust, with no Python. ocoeco builds on it, as Truelink will. After the wrap-up pass, the focus.

title: tad kept current in each repository
note: bin/update-pins.sh and consumers in tad's repository: for each repository the pin moved, the data re-canonicalized and the documents re-rendered by the new tad, landed through land so its own CI decides. First run: tad 0.2.0 (the notice names tad). Next: the lab machine's weekly timer.

title: Pages rendered from the data
note: tad renders every table as pages; matrices from the schema's shape.

title: Presentation declared as data
note: Page introductions, groupings by a field with headings, relation labels in words (Serves / Served by), field labels (Watch out, Also known as), combined fields (an origin line), ordering - declared in tables.toml, so the canon's own renderer (and DuckDB with it) can retire with its pages byte-identical.

title: Documents rendered from data
note: tad render: one page per table, Markdown and reStructuredText, every shape the Python renderer detects (relations, sources and citations, grids, the about page). Proven byte for byte against today's Python renderer: 74 documents across the four repositories, both formats.

title: tad as a rhizcut in every repository
note: Instead of a copied subtree of a dist branch: an owned, patchable rhizoid module. Needs rhizoid v1.

title: tad in Rust, formats unchanged
note: The same data, sturdier machinery; the observatory's engine already reads tad data in Rust.

title: Gatherers as standard parts of tad
note: CI jobs and hooks that read a project's real files, test results and releases into its tad data, the same way in every repository.

title: The four repositories switched; Python gone
note: All four repositories run on tad in Rust (2026-11-11): the playbook, Rhizoid, the phone project (its feeds kept their SQL, run by DuckDB's pinned standalone binary, proven to give the same rows) and the canon (its own renderer kept, its pages byte-identical). The Python engine retired from this repository; tad released by release-please and the package conveyor.

title: ocoeco builds on tad
note: ocoeco's shared shapes as a tad declaration; ocoeco note and check through tad's library.
